A report containing the sightings and traces of the legendary monster Bigfoot (Sasquatch) in Montana and Oregon, USA, has recently been released and is a hot topic.

The Guardian, a British daily, reported on the 22nd (local time) that the U.S. Forest Service has recently released reports and traces of big foot-related reports. Bigfoot originated from the legend that giant furry creatures that walk upright in the forests of northwestern North America.

A 1982 report released this time showed wildlife biologist Rodney Johnson examining footprints found in three Humortila National Forests in northeastern Oregon. Johnson judged that it was not a sign of Sasquatch, citing that his stride was constant even on the slope and that his footprints were not left deep in the mud at two points. Korea Forest Service investigators also dismissed the incident in a follow-up report, evaluating the footprints to the effect that they were fabricated.

The Forest Service also released local Montana newspaper reports in 2003, testimony that they saw a bear-like creature near a Montana creek, and records that Montana resident Leo Kinney said in 1980 that he encountered traces, odors and sounds of upright walking life while searching for elk bodies.

Witnesses are continuing in North America. In June, two creatures of different sizes and colors were reported to have been seen rummaging through piles of garbage in rural Ontario, Canada, and more than 16,000 related reports were accumulated in the Big Foot Mapping Project, which collects records of unidentified sightings of life.
